strategies.name: Naive Sequential All-Reduce Chain
strategies.desc: Directly implements the reference algorithm with 8 sequential all-reduce calls, each preceded by local bidiagonal coupling and followed by inverse coupling. 8 collective dispatches total. Represents the baseline: maximum clarity, no optimization, highest latency due to sequential synchronization barriers.

strategies.name: Reduce-Scatter + AllGather Decomposition
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing each rank to own and compute only its shard during the coupling operations. 16 collective dispatches (8 RS + 8 AG), but reduces per-stage communication volume and enables parallel local computation on disjoint shards, trading dispatch count for smaller per-collective payload.

strategies.name: Fused Coupling with Batched All-Reduce
strategies.desc: Combine multiple stages by computing several forward coupling transformations locally, then batch multiple independent all-reduces together if the hardware supports multi-tensor collectives or by concatenating buffers. Target 2-4 collective dispatches instead of 8, trading increased local computation and memory for fewer synchronization points.

strategies.name: Pipeline with Async All-Reduce Overlap
strategies.desc: Issue all-reduce asynchronously (if supported) and overlap computation of inverse coupling from stage i with communication of stage i+1. Still 8 dispatches but overlaps compute/communication, hiding latency behind local bidiagonal operations. Requires careful buffer management to avoid read-after-write hazards.

strategies.name: Hierarchical Two-Level Reduction Pattern
strategies.desc:
Exploit multi-node topology by splitting into intra-node (cores_per_device×num_devices per node) and inter-node all-reduces. Perform 8 stages where each uses node-local reduction, cross-node reduction, then broadcast back. Approximately 24 dispatches (8×3 levels) but optimized for network topology, reducing cross-node bandwidth pressure.
